question: to the Commission Lynn Boylan (The Left) Subject:
Early 2026 saw multi-country recalls of infant formula after the toxin cereulide was detected in batches of multiple international brands. In response to these recalls: 1.

Have all Member States classified food poisoning caused by cereulide as a notifiable disease, and have they ensured that notification and guidance have been provided to frontline healthcare professionals, parents and caregivers?

Have all Member States adopted a clinical pathway for investigating and testing cases, including a retrospective analysis of gastrointestinal illness data, and will the Commission publish a consolidated EU-wide epidemiological assessment based on national investigations?

Given that 21 of the 23 Rapid Alert System for Food and Feed (RASFF) notifications related to this incident were classified as ‘potentially serious’, with two issued on 1 May 2026 reclassified as ‘serious’, can the Commission comment as to the reasons for this escalation in risk classification, the additional steps taken in response to the reclassification, and whether it considers the existing RASFF classification framework adequate for incidents involving a product that is the sole source of nutrition for vulnerable infants?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.8.2026) 1. At the time of publication of the joint Rapid Outbreak Assessment (ROA) by the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) and the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) on 19 February 2026, which consolidated the available evidence, food poisoning caused by cereulide was not a notifiable disease in most EU/EEA1 countries. The organisation of national disease notification systems and communication of public health guidance are the responsibility of Member States. The ECDC supported Member States by facilitating information exchange through EpiPulse, publishing a European outbreak case definition on 6 March 2026, and providing scientific support. 2. Clinical pathways, diagnostic procedures, and retrospective analyses fall within Member States’ competences. The Commission does not systematically collect information on these measures. At the time of publication of the ROA, cereulide toxin testing in human (faecal) samples was not routinely available in clinical laboratories across Member States. The ECDC supported Member States by providing access to such testing through a contracted laboratory. 3. RASFF2 notifications 2026.38623 and 2026.38634 were submitted by Ireland as alert notifications with a ‘serious risk’ classification. This was a decision of the Irish authorities. These notifications were handled like previous cereulide notifications. All Alert notifications require rapid action by the network.

1 European Economic Area. 2 Rapid Alert System for Food and Feed. 3 https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/rasff-window/screen/notification/841471. 4 https://webgate.ec.europa.eu/rasff-window/screen/notification/841474.
